answer: Seed-bound attestation defeats precomputed farms. With words like opal, garden and pearl, every valid answer carries a tag H(seed, author secret, text). The seed stays hidden until the challenge opens, so a farm of stockpiled essays cannot stamp a valid tag afterward; forging one needs the author's secret. Each identity must compose freshly against the actual words and sign it. One template reused across clones shares one tag and is flagged as a copy. The attacker pays N genuine seed-specific compositions plus one secret key per identity, no stockpile or parallelism discount.
